# singlestoredb_private_connection_v2 (Resource)

Manage a private connection for a SingleStoreDB cluster with the v2 Management API. Import reads the connection by ID. `cluster_id` comes from that response, so a response that omits it cannot be imported. Changing `cluster_id`, `type`, `service_name`, `kai_endpoint_id`, `sql_port`, or `web_socket_port` replaces the connection. `allow_list` and `supported_cross_regions` can be updated in place.

## Example Usage

```terraform
provider "singlestoredb" {
  // The SingleStoreDB Terraform provider uses the SINGLESTOREDB_API_KEY environment variable for authentication.
  // Please set this environment variable with your SingleStore Management API key.
  // You can generate this key from the SingleStore Portal at https://portal.singlestore.com/organizations/org-id/api-keys.
}

resource "singlestoredb_cluster" "this" {
  name            = "cluster-1"
  project_name    = "Standard Project"
  size            = "S-00"
  firewall_ranges = ["0.0.0.0/0"] // Ensure restrictive ranges for production environments.
  expires_at      = "2222-01-01T00:00:00Z"
  cloud_provider  = "AWS"
  region_name     = "us-east-1"
}

resource "singlestoredb_private_connection_v2" "this" {
  cluster_id = singlestoredb_cluster.this.id
  allow_list = "651246146166"
  type       = "INBOUND"
}

output "private_connection_id" {
  value = singlestoredb_private_connection_v2.this.id
}

output "endpoint" {
  value = singlestoredb_private_connection_v2.this.endpoint
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cluster_id` (String) The ID of the cluster to connect with.

### Optional

- `allow_list` (String) The private connection allow list. This is the account ID for AWS, the subscription ID for Azure, and the project name for GCP. Required for an inbound connection unless `kai_endpoint_id` is set. Not allowed for an outbound connection.
- `kai_endpoint_id` (String) VPC Endpoint ID for an inbound SingleStore Kai connection. Cannot be combined with `allow_list`.
- `service_name` (String) The name of the private connection service. Required for an outbound connection. The API assigns it for an inbound connection.
- `sql_port` (Number) The SQL port. Defaults to 3306. A custom port is sent only when it is not 3306, because the API rejects a port when custom sockets are not enabled.
- `supported_cross_regions` (List of String) Additional regions allowed to reach this private connection. An update replaces the list. Omit the argument, or set it to an empty list, to remove every region.
- `type` (String) The private connection type, `INBOUND` or `OUTBOUND`.
- `web_socket_port` (Number) The websockets port. Defaults to 443. A custom port is sent only when it is not 443, because the API rejects a port when custom sockets are not enabled.

### Read-Only

- `active_at` (String) The timestamp of when the private connection became active.
- `created_at` (String) The timestamp of when the private connection was created.
- `deleted_at` (String) The timestamp of when the private connection was deleted.
- `endpoint` (String) The service endpoint.
- `id` (String) The unique identifier of the private connection.
- `outbound_allow_list` (String) The account ID which must be allowed for outbound connections.
- `status` (String) The status of the private connection.
- `updated_at` (String) The timestamp of when the private connection was updated.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = singlestoredb_private_connection_v2.this
  id = "26d4b214-ce96-445a-95d2-0980697d8fce"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import singlestoredb_private_connection_v2.this 26d4b214-ce96-445a-95d2-0980697d8fce
```
